chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not rise from a gathering, even if it was small, until he sought forgiveness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, twenty-five times.
ai.seo_question: How many times did the Prophet seek forgiveness after leaving a gathering?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) consistent practice of seeking forgiveness twenty-five times upon concluding any gathering, underscoring the Shia emphasis on humility and spiritual vigilance even in minor social interactions. Scholars note this practice as a model for maintaining spiritual purity and acknowledging potential minor shortcomings in discourse, reinforcing the concept of *istighfar* as a continuous state of being rather than merely a response to major sins. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to cultivate a habit of self-reflection and divine connection at the end of every communal engagement.
